tool_input.command: find routes -type f | xargs -I{} echo {}; echo "---"; cat routes/auth.js 2>/dev/null; find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -name "*.ts" -path "*routes*" -print 2>/dev/null
git stash && bun test 2>&1 | tail -40; git stash pop

result: The root cause: `routes/admin.ts` defined `registerAdminRoutes` (mounting `GET /admin/posts` behind the `auth` middleware alias) but `routes/web.ts` never imported or called it, so the route was never registered — hence the 404 for everyone, guests included. I fixed `routes/web.ts` to import and invoke `registerAdminRoutes(router)` alongside the existing `registerAuthRoutes(router)` call, then regenerated the codegen manifests (`.guren/routes.gen.ts`, `.guren/api-client.gen.ts`) and added `tests/AdminPostController.test.ts` covering both the guest-redirect-to-login case and the signed-in listing (with author data). `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (4 pass), and `bunx guren check` all pass, and `guren check` now reports the `routes/admin.ts` wiring as green.
